To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have defined a distance metric to assess similarity between machined parts based on machining feature information and we have developed algorithms to assess similarity between parts and to identify machined parts in the database that are similar from the machining effort perspective to a given query machined part.

we have defined a distance measure between two sets of machining feature vectors to assess shape similarity and we have defined a method to transform the feature vectors of one part with respect to the feature vectors of the other part so that the distance between the two parts is minimized.
we present algorithms for identifying machineable parts in a database based on their feature-based similarity.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following: (a) identifying machining features from a solid model of a part; (b) extracting reduced feature vectors for a given machining feature; (c) aligning the reduced feature vectors for the given machining feature with those in the database; (d) assessing the similarity between two sets of aligned feature vectors and (e) rank ordering machined parts in the database that are similar in shape to a given query machining feature.
the development of an algorithm that can be used to assess the similarity in terms of machining effort between machined prismatic parts.
developing algorithms for assessing the similarity of two parts in terms of the cost of machining them.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the algorithms presented in this paper are useful to estimate machining cost of new parts that have similar machining features with respect to previously machined parts in the database.
the algorithms presented in this paper are useful for estimating the cost and time of machining a new part from the existing machined parts in the database.
the algorithms presented in this paper are useful in assessing the similarity between prismatic parts based on the machining feature information.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the similarity between two machined parts is assessed using a reduced set of machining feature information and the similarity assessment algorithm is based on the distance between the two reduced feature vectors.

we have defined a distance measure between two sets of machining feature vectors, and have developed a method for identifying machined part in a database that is similar to a given machined part based on machining effort.
we have developed algorithms for assessing the similarity between two machined parts in terms of machining effort.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the similarity of machined parts can be assessed based on their machining features, and this can be used for estimating the machining cost of a new part based on the cost of machining similar parts.
we can identify parts that are similar to the given query part based solely on the machining feature information of the parts.
machining feature-based similarity assessment can be used to identify similar previously machined parts and can be used to estimate the cost of a new part.
